Notepad will do, but be sure to change 'save as type:' to "all files"The class configs MUST be named:scout.cfgsoldier.cfgpyro.cfgdemoman.cfgheavyweapons.cfgengineer.cfgmedic.cfgsniper.cfgspy.cfgApart from scout.cfg, all these files need only 1 line of text that executes reset.cfgscout.cfg should read:Then we need reset.cfg which will undo the changes when we swap class:And that's it done. Bob's your uncle. Give it a try. I think it works pretty well in the grand scheme of things.

When you run TF2 it looks inC:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Team Fortress 2\tf\cfgforconfig.cfgwhich contains all the advanced settings you're talking about.If it can't find config.cfg then it runsconfig_default.cfgwhich is the most basic keybinds needed to play, and uses that to create a new config.cfg.So, the likelihood is that you've renamed, moved or deleted config.cfg, or maybe resaved it as a .txt file.(NB. config.cfg will currently exist in the above location because you've played the game and a new one has been created from config_default.cfg settings so don't let that fool you; you need to find your old config.cfg or whatever it's now called)So...finding it could be fun and time consuming or really easy.You can recreate most of it through advanced settings if all else fails.
